non_blocking_notes: Edge gating is vacuous: the graph has exactly one node, m4-s1, with depends_on []. There is no edge to refute and no second node that could require one. ids are m4-s1 with no gaps, duplicates, cycles, or cross-milestone references; repo is 'RivRetrieve'; no version bump or tag is scheduled.

Guard placement verified. `git show 1b903fa:src/rivretrieve/_internal/registry.py` shows _ProviderHandle.observations (line 96) -> _drive_engine -> driver.drive, and `git show 1b903fa:src/rivretrieve/_internal/driver.py` shows drive() performing only _make_fetch_window, _require_fetch_window_contains_requested, and plan_windows before `provider.fetch(...)`. `git grep -ln 'HttpClient|urllib|requests.|httpx' 1b903fa -- src` returns transport.py, generate_catalogue.py scripts, usgs_nwis/fetch.py, and the ca_eccc/pl_imgw observation_clients; of the two providers registered with engine stages (discovery.py:247 usgs_nwis, discovery.py:317 ca_eccc) both reach I/O only inside their own fetch(). ProviderStages.fetch (driver.py:93-107) is genuinely the first source-call seam; the step names it correctly.

Recording-fake mechanism confirmed feasible without network. registry.register stores `stages = engine_provider_module` (registry.py:258) and drive calls `provider.fetch(...)` by attribute at call time; usgs_nwis/module.py and ca_eccc/module.py both re-export `fetch` as a module-level attribute, so monkeypatching module.fetch substitutes the seam. tests/test_internal_registry.py already registers _EngineModule-style fakes via engine_provider_module (lines 255, 424, 573, 703), and tests/conftest.py exposes RegisteredStub. Call counting through the existing seam needs no new machinery.

The Cartesian claim is TRUE at the ref. engine ObservationRequest carries `stations: tuple[str, ...]` and `products: tuple[ProductId, ...]` as independent axes (observations.py ObservationRequest; driver.py passes request.stations and request.products to fetch), and usgs_nwis/fetch.py loops `for station_id in stations: for product_id, ... in resolved_products:` — a sparse (station, product) series set does expand to the full product. A recording fake counting (station_id, product_id) pairs would detect a Cartesian regression, so the acceptance evidence bites.

Sparse routing will require the executor to choose between changing the ProviderStages.fetch signature (touching thirteen provider fetch implementations) and issuing several drive() calls per provider grouped so no unselected pair is requested, then merging the within-provider provenance/issues/raw into one ObservationResult. The step leaves that open. That is executor latitude, not a defect — but it is the largest unpriced cost in the step, and within-provider merging must not be read as licence to merge across providers.

Singular provenance verified: ObservationProvenance.provider_id: ProviderId with license and citation as single optional strings, RawPayload.provider_id: ProviderId, ObservationResult with exactly data/provenance/issues/raw. ObservationDataSchema is the five ADR-0006 columns and validate_observation_data raises ObservationDataSchemaError on any extra column, so a provider_id observation column is rejected outright rather than by convention.

ADR-0016 handling already exists and the step preserves rather than reimplements it: docs/adr/0016-a-requested-window-is-wall-clock.md is tracked at the ref, and observations._normalize_window_endpoint raises InvalidObservationRequestError on any tz-aware datetime or ISO string, expands a bare date to time.min/time.max for start/end (closed at both ends), and rejects start > end.

Scope boundaries hold: the step ships only fetch and fetch_by_provider, states raw=/on_issue=/RawMode are m5's, and explicitly forbids adding m7's map name or deleting any m9-owned legacy name. tests/test_package.py's exact-name assertion currently lists the fifteen names given as ground truth, so the described edit (add exactly fetch and fetch_by_provider) is the whole change to that assertion. Nothing from vision Scope-Out (bounding box, record_covers, source='live') appears.

Single-step decomposition survives. Splitting fetch from fetch_by_provider is not provably merge-green in isolation: fetch's mixed-provider error must name fetch_by_provider and direct the caller to it, so a fetch-only step would ship an error message pointing at a function that does not exist. The two are one guard and its escape hatch.

Acceptance feasibility caveat for the executor, not a defect: ca_eccc's real fetch reads a cached HYDAT SQLite that will be absent under a no-network executor and returns a HYDAT_NOT_AVAILABLE issue with zero payloads. The two-provider fetch_by_provider evidence must therefore run against substituted stages, which the step's recording-fake framing already implies.
summary: m4's graph is a single node with no edges, so there is nothing to refute and no missing edge is possible. Every load-bearing claim in m4-s1 survives source at 1b903fa: ProviderStages.fetch really is the first source-call seam on the observation path (drive performs only window arithmetic before it, and no registered engine provider touches transport earlier), the recording fake is constructible through the existing engine_provider_module seam that tests already use, the Cartesian claim is literally true in usgs_nwis/fetch.py's nested station-by-product loop, provenance and RawPayload are singular, the five-column frame rejects extra columns outright, and ADR-0016 wall-clock/closed-endpoint/zone-refusal handling already exists to be preserved. The step defers raw=/on_issue=/RawMode to m5, deletes no legacy name, and its scope is coextensive with the milestone. Splitting fetch from fetch_by_provider would ship an error message naming a nonexistent function, so the single step is justified on source rather than taste. APPROVE.
